newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: COMMONWEALTH GAMES CHIEF WITHDRAWS RESIGNATION.
newsitem.headline: COMMONWEALTH GAMES CHIEF WITHDRAWS RESIGNATION.

text.p: Commonwealth Games chief Retired-General Hashim Mohamed Ali withdraw his resignation on Tuesday one day after announcing he was quitting after criticism from two cabinet ministers.
The executive chairman of the 1998 Commonwealth Games organising committee said he had changed his mind after meeting acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Tuesday.
"If you want to know what changed my mind, here again with the greatest respect, it was the acting Prime Minister," Hashim told a news conference.
Hashim said Anwar had asked him to consider the damage that would be caused to the Games and the country if he resigned now. Kuala Lumpur will host the Games from September 11-21 next year.

Youth and Sports Minister Muhyiddin Yassin and Culture, Arts and Tourism Minister Sabbaruddin Chik had criticised the company organising the Games, Sukom 98, for what they said was its failure to publicise the biggest sporting event to be held in Malaysia.
Sabbaruddin had been especially blunt, accusing company executives of being more interested in travelling first class on overseas trips than in discharging their duties.
Hashim said on Tuesday the criticisms had demoralised his staff and part of the reason he changed his mind about quitting was that Sukom 98 board members were ready to resign as well.
Sabbaruddin told reporters on Monday he apologised for causing Hashim any offense but stood by his criticisms.
Hashim said on Tuesday, Sabbaruddin had not conveyed any regrets to him personally.

Some 100,000 visitors are expected for the Games, which cap a massive building programme in and around the Malaysian capital, including new hotels, a $3.5 billion new airport, an overhead rail transit system and other transport projects.
